title: Blur nearby pixels
summary: Blurring combines neighbouring pixel values to soften local changes. A kernel is the small neighbourhood used for the calculation.
introduction: Blurring combines neighbouring pixel values to soften local changes. A kernel is the small neighbourhood used for the calculation. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Blurring combines neighbouring pixel values to soften local changes. A kernel is the small neighbourhood used for the calculation.

blocks.code:
import cv2
import numpy as np

image = np.zeros((5, 5), dtype=np.uint8)
image[2, 2] = 255
blurred = cv2.GaussianBlur(image, (3, 3), 0)
print(int(blurred[2, 2]) < 255, int(blurred[2, 1]) > 0)
blocks.title: Blur nearby pixels

blocks.text: The output is True True. Some brightness spreads from the centre to nearby pixels, so the centre becomes dimmer and its neighbour becomes brighter.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Try a 5 by 5 kernel and inspect how far the brightness spreads.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: A blur can hide useful detail as well as noise.
For more detail later, use this [OpenCV further reading](https://docs.opencv.org/4.x/d6/d00/tutorial_py_root.html).
